title: Split WMBTs that exceed 5 acceptances or mix concerns (advisory)

facts.note: Fires when the planner authors or edits a WMBT artifact.
Planning task mentions WMBTs or their acceptances.
WMBT is created or its acceptance list/statement changes.
Needs a per-WMBT acceptance counter; the schema does not enforce the cap (wmbt.schema.json is not a file-level gate).

Whether a statement mentions multiple dimensions, involves different actors+actions, or mixes ALL/ANY gates needs semantic judgement. divergent_gates could become observable with a gate-value reader over acceptances.
Keep-together cases (same outcome at UI/API/DB with gate ALL; sequential steps of one process) need semantic judgement; they suppress split-trigger findings.

fires: A WMBT is authored with 6 or more acceptances (if it also matches a keep-together case, the source does not say which wins — see verifier_detail[3]).
A WMBT statement mentions multiple dimensions.
Some acceptances of a WMBT are gated ALL while others are gated ANY.
doesNotFire: Split-trigger findings for a WMBT whose acceptances assert the same outcome at UI, API and DB layers with gate ALL (single_truth_multiple_layers).
Split-trigger findings for a WMBT whose acceptances are sequential steps of one coherent process (coherent_sequence).

given: You are authoring or revising a WMBT and its acceptances. This is advisory guidance, not schema-enforced.
when: The WMBT has more than 5 acceptances, or its statement mentions multiple dimensions, involves different actors+actions, or combines divergent gates (ALL vs ANY).
then: Split it into separate WMBTs so none exceeds 5 acceptances and none mixes dimensions, different actors+actions, or ALL/ANY gates.
prefer: Treat more than 5 acceptances as a signal of mixed concerns and split by concern.
Split along every trigger present: separate WMBTs per dimension, per distinct actor+action pairing, and per gate type (ALL vs ANY); re-check each resulting WMBT against all triggers.

If an over-cap WMBT is one truth across UI/API/DB (gate ALL) or one coherent sequence, flag the cap-vs-keep-together conflict for review instead of silently choosing; the source does not define precedence.
avoid: Packing more than 5 acceptances into one WMBT.
A WMBT statement that mentions multiple dimensions.
Mixing ALL-gated and ANY-gated acceptances in one WMBT.
Splitting only to get under the cap while the resulting WMBTs still mix concerns, or splitting one truth or one sequence apart.
unless: single_truth_multiple_layers: the acceptances assert the same outcome at UI/API/DB with gate ALL — keep together.
coherent_sequence: the acceptances are sequential steps of one process — keep together.
why: Beyond 5 acceptances, or mixed dimensions, different actors+actions, or divergent gates, indicate mixed concerns that should be separate WMBTs.
evidence: Each WMBT has <= 5 acceptances, or an over-cap keep-together WMBT is explicitly flagged as a cap-vs-keep-together conflict.

No WMBT exhibits a split trigger (statement mentioning multiple dimensions, different actors+actions, ALL vs ANY gates), unless a keep-together case applies (same outcome at UI/API/DB with gate ALL, or sequential steps of one process).
verifier_detail: acceptance_cap: the per-WMBT acceptance ceiling; maximum = 5. Count > 5 is a finding.
split_trigger: when to split a WMBT; allowed values = mixed_dimensions (statement mentions multiple dimensions), multiple_actors (different actors+actions), divergent_gates (ALL vs ANY).
when_to_keep_together values: single_truth_multiple_layers (same outcome at UI/API/DB, gate ALL), coherent_sequence (sequential steps of one process). These suppress split_trigger findings.

Unresolved source ambiguity: the source does not state whether the keep-together cases also override acceptance_cap. Treat both keep-together cases identically; for an over-cap WMBT matching either case, report the cap finding as advisory with the keep-together case noted, rather than assigning precedence.
Disposition: advisory guidance, not schema-enforced — wmbt.schema.json is not applied as a file-level gate (see #760). Report findings as advisory, not blocking.

Original name: WMBT splitting rules. Original statement: Keep <=5 acceptances per WMBT; split on mixed dimensions, multiple actors, or divergent gates; keep together for single-truth-multiple-layers or a coherent sequence.

additions.text: Activation facts, fires/doesNotFire and observer notes; keep-together doesNotFire entries are scoped to split-trigger findings with no acceptance-count qualification.
additions.justification: Required by the target schema; derived from the source triggers and keep-together cases, treating both cases symmetrically.

additions.text: Split along every trigger present and re-check each resulting WMBT; flag the cap-vs-keep-together conflict instead of silently choosing.
additions.justification: Reviewer usability risks (multiple coexisting triggers; unclear cap precedence). The source does not define precedence, so the rewrite surfaces the ambiguity rather than inventing a rule. Also reflected in verifier_detail[3] and evidence[0].

additions.text: No split proposed: the cap and the three triggers are the same decision (when to split a WMBT); keep-together cases are its exceptions.
